title: Technical English — Course 5, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 14

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the proposals be reviewed?
tasks.audioText: The engineering manager will review improvement proposals on Friday at eleven. Students should bring a one-page proposal and a short evidence summary. Each proposal should describe the current issue, the suggested change, expected benefits and possible limitations. The manager will ask how success could be measured and who would be responsible for reviewing the results.
options: On Friday at eleven
At the college library
At the town centre
At the bus station

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which proposal materials should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The engineering manager will review improvement proposals on Friday at eleven. Students should bring a one-page proposal and a short evidence summary. Each proposal should describe the current issue, the suggested change, expected benefits and possible limitations. The manager will ask how success could be measured and who would be responsible for reviewing the results.
options: On Friday
A one-page proposal and evidence summary
Next month
After the event

tasks.prompt: A proposal suggested changing the inspection-record template to reduce incomplete entries. The author used a sample audit to identify the most frequently missing fields and proposed adding clearer prompts. The proposal also noted that staff would need a short briefing before the new template was introduced. It recommended comparing record completeness before and after the change rather than assuming that the new format would solve every problem. Reading 1. What evidence supported the proposed change?
options: A supplier complaint about delivery time
A sample audit showing frequently missing fields
A staff rota showing shift preferences
A maintenance forecast showing expected workload

tasks.prompt: What additional action did the proposal identify?
options: A short staff briefing before introducing the template
A change to the supplier payment schedule
A replacement of the inspection equipment
Cancellation of the next sample audit

tasks.prompt: The proposal recommends ___ record completeness before and after the change.
options: comparing
compare
to comparing
compared

tasks.prompt: Choose TWO elements of a well-supported technical improvement proposal.
options: A promise that no limitations exist
A change with no identified owner
Evidence of the current issue
A method for measuring results

tasks.prompt: A formal suggestion for a change or course of action is a ___.
A proposal describes benefits but no way to measure them. What should you ask?
options: The benefits do not need to be measured.
How could we measure whether the proposed change has improved the process?
We should approve it immediately.
The current process does not matter.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of technical improvement proposal in a logical order.
options: Identify benefits, limitations and responsibilities
Describe the current issue with evidence
Define how results will be measured
Propose a specific change
correctOrder: Describe the current issue with evidence
Define how results will be measured

tasks.prompt: Write 100–120 words proposing a technical process improvement. Include evidence of the current issue, a suggested change, a limitation and a way to measure success.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total. Score each criterion 0–2: (1) Current issue and evidence — 2: describes the process issue with relevant baseline evidence; 1: partial; 0: absent. (2) Proposed change — 2: presents a practical change linked to the evidence; 1: partial; 0: unsupported or vague. (3) Limitation and success measure — 2: identifies a limitation and a measurable indicator for reviewing effectiveness; 1: mentions one; 0: neither. (4) English — 2: coherent proposal and accurate process-improvement vocabulary; 1: errors but meaning clear; 0: meaning frequently unclear.
